predecessors.name: Holy Roman Empire
predecessors.text: the lands round Hohenbaden Castle: 'it was named a margraviate in 1112'

successors.name: Electorate of Baden
successors.text: 'The restored Margraviate of Baden was elevated to the status of electorate in 1803' with the Prince-Bishopric of Constance, parts of the Rhenish Palatinate and smaller districts as additions

ledger.x: 1219: 'In 1219 he moved his seat of power to Pforzheim.'
1565: 'The residence moved from Pforzheim to Karlsburg Castle in Durlach in 1565' (Baden-Durlach line; the Baden-Baden line resided at Baden-Baden until 1705, then Rastatt).
1803: 'The restored Margraviate of Baden was elevated to the status of electorate in 1803.'

wars.name: Mainz Archbishops' Feud (Baden's part)
wars.outcome: 'He had to surrender several of his territories to the Electoral Palatinate and its allies' (Margrave Charles I, defeated in 1462).

wars.name: Occupation of Baden-Baden by Baden-Durlach
wars.outcome: 'Baden-Durlach occupied Baden-Baden from 1594 to 1622'; it ended after the defeat at Wimpfen on 6 May 1622.

wars.name: Nine Years' War devastation of Baden
wars.outcome: 'In 1689, Mélac systematically burnt all the cities and villages of Baden, except for Gernsbach'; Pforzheim and Durlach were burned.

certainty.note: The pages give castles, towns and cadet lines, not boundaries; the only dated acquisition is half of Lahr-Mahlberg in 1442 and the Peace of Westphalia restored the 1550 situation.
